master_prompt.title: PROPERTY EMPIRE 3D - AUTONOMOUS WEB BROWSER GAME DEVELOPMENT
master_prompt.agent_role: Autonomous Senior Web Game Developer, TypeScript Engineer, Three.js 3D Developer, Multiplayer Engineer, AI Developer, UI/UX Designer and QA Engineer
master_prompt.primary_instruction: Build an actually playable, polished Monopoly-inspired 3D BROWSER game that launches via URL in desktop and mobile browsers. Write real files, execute builds and automated tests, fix defects and verify in-browser play. Preserve complete core rules, bots, and LAN/hotspot human multiplayer. Do not stop at plans or pseudocode.

execution_mode.ask_for_confirmation: Only for destructive operations, security-sensitive changes, unavailable credentials, license acceptance or decisions that cannot safely be made automatically.
execution_mode.install_missing_dependencies: Install using trustworthy official sources when environment permissions allow. Never silently modify unrelated software.
execution_mode.goal: Deliver a runnable web application, local-network multiplayer room server, tested production web bundle, and clear launch instructions; no APK.
priority_order: Working browser gameplay and accessible controls

project.name: Property Empire 3D
project.secondary_platform: Windows/macOS/Linux browser testing; phone browsers on the same LAN
project.orientation: Landscape preferred for mobile, but responsive layouts must also work in portrait
project.internet_required: No external internet required for locally served games; LAN multiplayer requires reachable local Node server, while solo can function offline after assets are cached
project.game_type: Turn-based property trading and economic strategy board game
project.target_experience: Attractive, responsive, no-install 3D board game accessible by local URL or deployed HTTPS URL.

intellectual_property.requirement: Use original branding, illustrations, icons and 3D assets.
avoid: Third-party copyrighted game assets without permission
intellectual_property.board_policy: Implement configurable, classic-inspired rules with an original board theme and original names. Do not assume distinctive Monopoly assets are freely reusable.

technology.three_d: Three.js (WebGL) with simple procedural low-poly geometries
technology.ui: HTML/CSS/TypeScript components; avoid heavyweight UI framework unless justified
technology.animation: requestAnimationFrame + Three.js animation/tweens; optional lightweight GSAP only if justified
technology.networking: Node.js + ws WebSocket server using browser-compatible WebSocket protocol
technology.network_model: Authoritative local Node.js room server, not a browser host. Server validates every command and owns RNG and bot turns.
technology.offline_solo: Same pure TypeScript rules engine running inside browser for solo play with bots; no backend required
technology.shared_rules: Reusable TypeScript game-core library consumed by browser solo client and Node multiplayer server
technology.local_data: IndexedDB for browser savegames with schema validation; localStorage for lightweight settings
technology.testing: Vitest for deterministic rules/bots; Playwright for browser flows; WebSocket integration tests for multiplayer
technology.build: Vite production static frontend assets and Node.js server application; npm scripts
technology.runtime: Recent stable LTS Node.js and modern Chromium, Firefox, Safari and mobile Chromium/Safari

initial_actions: Inspect workspace, available Node.js/npm/pnpm, Git and browser automation tooling.
Initialize web monorepo or simple workspace; inspect existing files before changing them.
Install only necessary trusted npm dependencies when permitted.
Create frontend, shared core and LAN server modules.
Start dev server, run tests and launch automated browsers when available.
Provide exact local and LAN URLs and instructions to allow phone browsers on Wi-Fi/hotspot.

requirements.browser: Modern WebGL-capable browser with JavaScript enabled
requirements.same_network: For local rooms, all phones/computers must reach the same host computer over Wi-Fi or hotspot. Router isolation/firewall may block this.
requirements.ports: Document frontend and WebSocket ports; configure host binding to 0.0.0.0 only for trusted LAN usage.
requirements.no_android: Never install Android SDK, Godot export templates, adb, Java or create APKs as part of this project.

development_environment.failure_policy: If browser, network or installation testing is unavailable, implement/test all available layers and precisely report what was not verified.

overall_style.description: Premium-looking yet simple stylized 3D tabletop board game.
overall_style.art_style: Low-poly, friendly, clean, colorful and slightly rounded.
overall_style.lighting: Soft ambient lighting with gentle directional shadows.
overall_style.materials: Simple colors with modest roughness and highlights.

palette.color_group_policy: Use easily distinguishable property colors, supported by labels and icons.

camera.default: Stable 3D isometric perspective showing the whole board.
camera.rotate: Mouse drag or touch drag, optionally limit tilt; do not interfere with buttons
camera.zoom: Mouse wheel, pinch zoom and +/- buttons
camera.focus_property: Smoothly focus selected 3D tile with UI-aware framing
camera.accessibility: Allow camera motion and animation speed to be reduced.

board.construction: Programmatically create the board from data-driven space definitions.
board.design: Clear perimeter tiles with a visually interesting but inexpensive central area.
board.readability: Prefer short labels and larger interactive information panels instead of tiny text.
board.center_area: Original Property Empire emblem, decorative city illustration or minimalist logo.

3d_models.player_token: Simple colored pawn or original stylized token.
3d_models.houses: Small colorful low-poly houses built using cubes and roof primitives.
3d_models.hotel: Larger rounded or tiered low-poly building.
3d_models.dice: Two lightweight 3D cubes with clearly visible numbers or pips.
3d_models.environment: Subtle tabletop, simple background gradient and soft shadows.
3d_models.generation_rule: Use procedural shapes and built-in meshes first. Do not require Blender or external asset downloads for core functionality.

dice_roll.implementation: Generate valid dice values in the authoritative rules engine before starting the visual animation.

token_movement.visual_style: Small hop or smooth sliding movement.

property_purchase.effect: Property highlight and subtle celebratory particles.

rent_payment.effect: Animated money transfer indicator and balance updates.

buildings.effect: Quick scale-up animation when a house or hotel appears.

turn_transition.effect: Highlight active player and update turn banner.

bankruptcy.effect: Brief visual notification without interrupting game state.

performance.thermal_policy: Do not run expensive simulations or unnecessary rendering when waiting for a player.
performance.webgl_context_loss: Gracefully handle context loss and offer a reload recovery.
performance.responsive_resize: Recalculate renderer, camera aspect and UI safely on resize and rotation.

splash.behavior: Load essential resources and proceed to the main menu.

main_menu.design: Simple polished layout with an animated low-poly board background.

multiplayer_lobby.behavior: The host controls game configuration. Joining players can select their names and tokens.

components: Enter room code or invite link
Explain why a browser cannot join using UDP broadcast
join_game.behavior: Manual-IP joining must always be available even if automatic discovery fails.

layout.top: Player turn, active player and compact game status
layout.bottom: Roll Dice, Properties, Trade, Manage Assets, End Turn and Menu

requirements: Responsive desktop mouse/keyboard and mobile touch controls.
Keep the board legible at common desktop/tablet/phone screen sizes.
Allow zoom and property inspection rather than placing tiny dense labels everywhere.

game_rules.ruleset: Classic-inspired property trading rules, configured through data files.

board_spaces.configuration: Each space must have a unique ID, board index, display name, type and relevant properties.
board_spaces.initial_content: Populate a complete original 40-space board with internally consistent purchase prices, rents, mortgage amounts and group colors.
board_spaces.balance: Use conventional classic board-game economics as a starting point and keep numbers editable.

player_setup.start_player: Randomly select the initial player using the authoritative host.

turn_structure: Allow appropriate property management and trades
Handle another roll if doubles apply
Advance to the next active player

dice.dice_authority: Only the host generates final dice outcomes.
dice.randomness: Use the engine's RNG with appropriate initialization. Support injectable deterministic seeds for tests.

auction.payment_rule: A bid cannot exceed funds currently available for the transaction.
auction.end_condition: Highest remaining bidder wins, or property remains with Bank if all pass before any valid bid.
auction.multiplayer: Every client sees the same authoritative bidding state.

rent.full_color_group_bonus: Double undeveloped street base rent when the complete color group is owned and applicable conditions are satisfied.
rent.transport_rent: Depends on how many matching transport properties are owned.
rent.utility_rent: Depends on the dice result and utility ownership count.
rent.rent_claim: Automatically collect rent under selected rules, simplifying the browser experience.

building.building_sales: Sell buildings to the Bank for half purchase cost, following even-selling rules.
building.shortages: Do not create buildings beyond Bank supply. Support auctions for contested limited stock where applicable.

escape_options: Use Get Out of Jail Free card
Attempt doubles on up to three turns
jail.third_failure: Pay 50 and move using the third roll.
jail.doubles_escape: Move with the successful roll without receiving an additional roll.

cards.chance: Create a complete configurable deck of original events with movement, payments, rewards, repairs and Jail effects.
cards.community: Create a second original event deck with equivalent core mechanics.
cards.get_out_of_jail_free: Cards are held by players until used or traded and return to their appropriate deck.
cards.execution: The host resolves card effects; clients receive results.

mortgage.ownership_transfer: Implement the appropriate mortgage transfer interest rules.

supported_items: Tradable Get Out of Jail Free cards

bankruptcy.creditor_rules: Transfer assets to the creditor or return property to the Bank for auction depending on creditor type.

bot_system.purpose: Bots should behave like convincing casual human opponents and operate completely offline.

bot_count.architecture: Do not hardcode a small number of bots. Use dynamic player collections and configurable caps.
bot_count.experimental_high_player_counts: Potential future option; initial browser implementation supports a practical cap (default 8 total participants).

easy.purchase_strategy: Buy affordable properties with some randomness.

medium.purchase_strategy: Prefer color-group completion and properties with good returns.
medium.auction_strategy: Bid using estimated value and available cash.

hard.purchase_strategy: Estimate strategic value using ownership, opponents, expected rental value and liquidity.
hard.trade_strategy: Evaluate both immediate and long-term trade value.

save_system.format: Versioned JSON serialized into IndexedDB locally; atomic temp-and-rename JSON files on server
save_system.directory: IndexedDB database: property-empire-saves (frontend solo) and ./data/saves/ (LAN host process)
autosave: On page visibility change when safe (not sole guarantee)

file_integrity.atomic_write: Use IndexedDB transactions in browser and atomic replacement in Node server

multiplayer.resume_policy: Host may reopen a saved match and reconnect players into their original slots.

architecture.principle: Keep rules independent from graphics, UI, networking and bots.

modules.RulesEngine: Deterministic state transitions and legal action validation.
modules.TurnManager: Turn progression, dice rolls, doubles and Jail.
modules.BoardData: Loads and validates board spaces and property data.
modules.PropertyManager: Ownership, rent, group completion, mortgages and buildings.
modules.CardManager: Card decks, effects and held cards.
modules.NetworkManager: Browser WebSocket transport / Node room server; no ENet or Godot networking
modules.GameSession: Orchestrate solo local reducer versus remote WebSocket session
modules.SaveManager: IndexedDB local persistence plus Node host save files
modules.BoardRenderer3D: Three.js scene, meshes, camera, picking/raycasting and responsive render loop
modules.UIManager: HTML/CSS browser screens and accessible controls

state_machine.requirement: Define explicit legal transitions and prevent overlapping actions or duplicate processing.

design_rules: Game rules must be independently testable without rendering.
Use one canonical source of truth.
Use typed events and small interfaces rather than tightly coupled rendering modules.
Keep configuration outside the core rules engine.
Use strict TypeScript without implicit any.

project_structure.requirement: Keep rules shareable by client and Node server; Vite static assets separated from ws room server.

implementation_phases.name: Web toolchain and project setup
tasks: Create Vite/TypeScript frontend, game-core package and Node WebSocket server.
Implement valid HTML entry and startable web UI.
Configure npm scripts: dev, dev:lan, build, start:server, test, test:e2e, lint, typecheck.
Create responsive main menu and health endpoint.
acceptance: npm install and npm run dev work.
Browser opens home screen with no fatal console errors.
Typecheck passes.

implementation_phases.name: Complete rules engine
acceptance: A simulated full game completes without an infinite loop.
Financial conservation and legal action invariants are checked.
All important rules have automated tests.

implementation_phases.name: Three.js 3D board and browser graphics
tasks: Create a orbit-limited isometric perspective camera.
Ensure every board tile is visually distinct.
acceptance: Entire board is inspectable in browser.
Tokens and buildings appear at correct positions.
Pointer/touch raycasting selects tiles.
Renderer scales to mobile browser and handles resize.

implementation_phases.name: Gameplay user interface
tasks: Wire every control to real game logic.
acceptance: A human can complete a full match in browser.
Desktop mouse and mobile touch controls are usable.
No action depends on developer console commands.

implementation_phases.name: Bots
acceptance: Human versus bot matches run.
Multiple bots can play together.
Bots complete legal actions without deadlocks.

implementation_phases.name: LAN multiplayer over WebSockets
tasks: Implement authoritative Node WebSocket room server.
Create/join room by short code and browser invite URL.
Display the correct LAN host URL.
Connect browser clients via configurable WS URL.
Synchronize lobby, accepted commands and canonical snapshots.
Add mixed human/bot rooms and privacy-conscious local defaults.
Write server/client integration tests using multiple browser contexts.
Explain firewall, hotspot isolation and HTTPS/WSS.
acceptance: At least two independent browser clients can join a match in tests.
Server rejects illegal commands and client-authored dice.
Players see same positions, balances, purchases and phases.
Human and bot turns function together.

implementation_phases.name: Animations, sound and polish
acceptance: Animations represent the authoritative results.
Animations can be accelerated.
Gameplay remains functional with animations disabled.

implementation_phases.name: Save, resume and final testing
tasks: Verify desktop/mobile browser behavior and resizing.
acceptance: Saved games restore correctly.
No known critical blockers remain unreported.
Test results are documented.

implementation_phases.name: Production web build and browser delivery
tasks: Generate optimized frontend bundle with Vite.
Check dist output and server startup.
Test solo mode without a backend after assets load.
Test LAN host and two browser clients with reachable addresses.
Validate room links, reconnect and responsive touch layouts.
Provide npm commands to start local dev and production LAN services.
Provide optional HTTPS/WSS deployment guide without requiring hosted infrastructure.
acceptance: npm run build succeeds.
Static web build and server artifacts exist.
A browser can play solo.
LAN multiplayer works in tested network or is accurately marked unverified.

rules_tests: Players start with correct cash.
Dice always produce values from 1 through 6.
Movement wraps around 40 board spaces.
Passing GO awards the correct cash.
Direct transfer to Jail does not award GO cash.
Buying a property transfers the correct cash and ownership.
Declining a purchase starts an auction.
Auction winner pays the valid winning bid.
Unowned properties do not charge rent.
Mortgaged properties do not charge rent.
Monopoly ownership affects undeveloped rent correctly.
Houses and hotels increase rent.
Buildings follow even-building and even-selling requirements.
Building inventory cannot become negative.
Three consecutive doubles send a player to Jail.
Jail escape rules function correctly.
Card effects apply once.
Trade acceptance transfers exactly the agreed items.
Invalid trades are rejected.
Debt resolution and bankruptcy work.
Eliminated players receive no further turns.
Last solvent player wins.
bot_tests: Bot decisions never directly mutate unauthorized client state.
network_tests: Multiple clients receive correct initial state.
Disconnect handling does not corrupt game state.
browser_tests: Web app loads without uncaught JavaScript errors.
3D canvas initializes and responds to resize.
Mouse and touch interaction select board tiles.
Responsive HUD works on desktop and simulated mobile viewports.
Client-only solo match works without WebSocket service.
Reconnect flow restores active player identity.
Cross-origin and malformed WebSocket requests are appropriately rejected.

functional: No mocked multiplayer presented as functional.
No bots that merely skip turns.
No negative cash except explicitly modeled temporary debt resolution.
No double processing of network actions.
visual: No oversized dialogs blocking essential controls.
Provide visible keyboard focus and adequate contrast.
Canvas resolution and interaction scale gracefully to phones.
engineering: Remove temporary debug-only shortcuts from release behavior.

must_have: Node.js LAN room server with shareable room links
nice_to_have: Installable PWA and cached solo mode
do_not_build: Android APK or native app packaging

rules: Immediately inspect the workspace and tools.
Prefer completing core mechanics over polishing empty screens.
Run TypeScript typechecking, Vite builds, browser smoke tests and Vitest frequently.
Run automated rules tests as modules are implemented.
Keep the project launchable after major milestones.
Implement networking with real peers rather than simulated button demonstrations.
Run production frontend/server build after core functionality exists and again at the end.
Resolve build problems instead of merely describing them.
Read terminal output and fix actual errors.
Continue through phases without waiting for routine approval.
Record genuine limitations when external equipment or permissions are unavailable.

failure_handling.syntax_error: Inspect failing scripts, fix syntax and rerun validation.
failure_handling.missing_resource: Fix resource paths or create valid replacements.
failure_handling.missing_dependency: Attempt permitted official installation; otherwise document blocker.
failure_handling.network_error: Inspect logs and transport assumptions, then retry with localhost or available LAN peers.
failure_handling.time_or_context_limit: Leave a working checkpoint, current test report and exact next actions.
failure_handling.browser_render_failure: Check WebGL support, console errors, shader compilation, pixel ratio and fallback.
failure_handling.web_build_failure: Diagnose TypeScript/Vite/dependency failure, fix and rerun.
failure_handling.unavailable_physical_devices: Keep browser automated tests and record real phone/hotspot tests as not tested.

reporting.requirement: Status documents must reflect actual implementation and executed tests.

mandatory: Browser start, LAN joining and production deployment instructions
readme_sections: How to play solo entirely in browser
How to host a Wi-Fi browser game with Node
How to join via LAN/hotspot IP and room link
How to run dev/production web build

production_web.success_condition: Static bundle and executable server build exist and npm run build succeeds
production_web.smoke_test: Serve bundle and connect at least two browser test clients when possible

The main menu can launch a real match.
The board contains 40 correctly indexed spaces.
A human can roll dice and move a token.
Purchases and rent operate correctly.
Auctions, buildings, mortgages and trades operate correctly.
Jail and bankruptcy function correctly.
A match can be completed.
Bots can play full matches.
A LAN host and at least one client can exchange real game commands in a tested environment.
Human and bot players can coexist in a match.
State synchronization has been tested.
The board and dice have functioning 3D visuals.
Gameplay uses actual animated tokens.

The final report distinguishes verified results from untested features.

Desktop and mobile viewport layouts are usable.

browser_multiplayer.objective: Players on different browser devices join the same game over LAN, shared Wi-Fi or phone hotspot without external internet or a cloud account. A Node.js WebSocket server on a reachable host computer/device is mandatory for multiplayer; a browser tab cannot be an ENet/UDP listening server.

host_architecture.model: Authoritative Node.js process (NOT a browser peer host)
host_responsibilities: Manage rooms and player session tokens
Validate actions and prevent duplicate submissions
Maintain canonical match state and RNG
host_architecture.solo_exception: Solo games execute the exact shared core engine locally in the browser with no WebSocket server.

network.primary_transport: Browser WebSocket (ws:// on trusted HTTP LAN; wss:// behind HTTPS when hosted)
network.room_join: Short room code and direct invite URL, plus optional manual server URL
network.automatic_discovery: Do not assume browser UDP broadcast/mDNS APIs. No UDP discovery in version 1.
caveats: Browsers cannot expose raw UDP ENet sockets or run a normal listening WebSocket server.
For multiplayer launch Node.js server on PC/laptop/Raspberry Pi connected to same reachable LAN as players.
Client devices open a LAN URL such as http://192.168.1.10:5173; localhost on a phone means the phone, not the PC.
Expose/bind web and socket services on 0.0.0.0 for LAN only, and configure Windows Firewall as needed.
Some mobile hotspots or guest Wi-Fi isolate clients.
HTTPS pages cannot open insecure ws:// connections; use wss:// and appropriate proxy/deployment configuration.
PWA service worker offline caching enables solo after first successful load but does not magically make remote LAN multiplayer work without a server.

security.session_tokens: Generate cryptographically random reconnect tokens; do not log or include them in share URLs.
security.origin_checks: Check WebSocket origins against configured allowed origins.
security.input_validation: Validate schema, action ID, turn ownership, room membership and message size.
security.deployment: No open public unauthenticated server by default; LAN only unless user later chooses secure hosted mode.

disconnects.timeout_behavior: Pause or wait for a disconnected active human according to game settings.
disconnects.host_disconnect: In version 1 show that the room ended and retain the most recent host save. Host migration is not required.

final_instruction_to_claude_code: BEGIN IMPLEMENTATION NOW IN THE CURRENT LOCAL PROJECT OR CONNECTED WORKSPACE. Do not only provide a plan or samples. Write the full runnable TypeScript/Three.js/Vite project and Node WebSocket server. Develop deterministic shared rules and offline bots, responsive 3D UI, authoritative LAN multiplayer, browser/host save systems and tests. Launch services where tools permit, inspect real errors, repair failures, complete production builds and document exact launch URLs and commands. Do not generate an Android app or APK. Do not rely on GitHub Actions or remote deployment for local development. Commit useful checkpoints when Git is available. Distinguish actually tested behavior from unverified environments.

browser_launch_and_lan_instructions.expected_behavior: Start web server bound to 0.0.0.0 and local WebSocket host. Show localhost URL for host PC and LAN IP URL for phones. Each phone opens the web URL and enters/shared room code.
browser_launch_and_lan_instructions.security: Local LAN only by default; never silently port-forward or publicly expose the server.
browser_launch_and_lan_instructions.websocket_addressing: Prefer same-origin reverse proxy to /ws where available; otherwise derive ws URL from the HTTP page host with a configured port. Do not hardcode localhost in clients.
browser_launch_and_lan_instructions.hotspot: If laptop is hotspot host, clients must have client-to-host TCP access. Document host firewall rules and alternative direct Wi-Fi-router test.
browser_launch_and_lan_instructions.offline: Web assets can optionally use PWA cache for subsequent solo use; first visit requires files to be served, unless installed/cached.
